capabilities.description: Two-way watchlist and rating sync for a Letterboxd account, movies only, with the watchlist in Letterboxd's own order.

config_schema.title: Connect to Letterboxd
config_schema.description: Letterboxd blocks sign-ins from servers, so the plugin uses a cookie from your browser. Sign in at letterboxd.com, copy the value of the letterboxd.user cookie, and paste it in the box labeled API key below. Enter your username here, not your email. Silo stores both encrypted. When Letterboxd stops accepting the cookie, connect again with a new one. The watchlist and ratings sync; the other options on this page have no effect for Letterboxd.

fields.label: Username
fields.description: The name in your profile address, letterboxd.com/<username>/.

presentation.summary: Sync a Silo profile's watchlist and ratings with Letterboxd, movies only.
presentation.description_markdown: Imports the Letterboxd watchlist into Silo in Letterboxd's order, sends watchlist adds and removals made in Silo back to Letterboxd, syncs movie ratings both ways, and leaves series alone. Letterboxd has no public API for this, so the plugin uses the website the way a signed-in browser does.
presentation.setup_markdown:
Each Silo profile connects with its own Letterboxd account. Sign in at letterboxd.com in a browser and copy the value of the `letterboxd.user` cookie. Your username goes in the connection's username field and the cookie value in the field Silo labels API key. Silo stores both encrypted. The cookie gives full access to the account, so treat it like a password. When Letterboxd stops accepting it, connect again with a new one. The plugin needs no server-wide settings.

Turn on **Sync watchlist removals** so a film removed on one side is removed on the other. Ratings sync both ways in half stars. A rating made in Silo reaches Letterboxd once the profile has finished the film, because rating a film on Letterboxd also marks it watched.

The first sync looks up every watchlisted and rated film once, at about 1.5 seconds per film; later syncs take seconds.
